html:
The Huastec, who call themselves Teenek, are a Maya people of the Huasteca, the lowlands and hills near the Gulf of Mexico in today's San Luis Potosí and Veracruz. Their language is Mayan, but it split from the others very long ago, and they live far to the north of the main Maya lands of the Maya cities.

In the centuries before 1492 the Huastec built towns with round temple platforms and were known for their shell carving and stone sculpture. Their neighbours to the south were the Totonac. In the late 1400s the Aztec Triple Alliance conquered much of the Huasteca and took tribute from it.

Hernán Cortés subdued the region in 1522 and 1523. In the late 1520s its governor, Nuño de Guzmán, had thousands of Huastecs enslaved and shipped to the Caribbean. Today the Teenek still live in the Huasteca, and their language is spoken by over a hundred thousand people. Many Nahua live alongside them.
